story_type: uncrewed moon mission, launch to splashdown
hook: This spaceship went around the Moon with nobody inside.
narration: This spaceship went around the Moon with nobody inside.
It was Orion, flying an uncrewed test before NASA would trust it with astronauts.
It launched before two in the morning, on November sixteenth, 2022.
Twice, it swept within eighty miles of the lunar surface.
At its farthest, it was nearly two hundred seventy thousand miles from home.
[short pause] Coming home from the Moon is faster than coming home from orbit, so the heat shield takes a harder hit.
outcome: After twenty five and a half days, Orion came down under its parachutes and splashed into the Pacific Ocean.
title: Moon capsule flew with nobody aboard
description:
NASA's uncrewed Artemis I mission launched Orion on Nov. 16, 2022. Over 25.5 days it made two lunar flybys within 80 miles of the surface, traveled nearly 270,000 miles from Earth and splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.

question_comment: Would you have flown on the second flight, knowing the first had nobody aboard?

facts.claim: Launched 1:47 a.m. EST Nov. 16, 2022 from Kennedy
facts.source_quote: At 1:47 a.m. EST (6:47 UTC) on Nov. 16, 2022, NASA’s Orion spacecraft launched atop the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket from historic Launch Pad 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center
Over the course of 25.5 days, Orion performed two lunar flybys, coming within 80 miles (129 kilometers) of the lunar surface.
At its farthest distance during the mission, Orion traveled nearly 270,000 miles (435,000 kilometers) from our home planet.
NASA’s Orion spacecraft successfully completed a parachute-assisted splashdown in the Pacific Ocean
This will be an uncrewed flight test that will demonstrate the ability of the SLS rocket to safely carry the Orion spacecraft around the Moon

extra_sources.excerpt: This will be an uncrewed flight test that will demonstrate the ability of the SLS rocket to safely carry the Orion spacecraft around the Moon and its return and recovery to Earth for the agency’s Artemis Program.
